stories.headline: Hillyard: The Railroad Town Built by an Empire Builder
stories.dek: A prairie town took the name Hill's Yard whether Jim Hill liked it or not, and for ninety years its shops built and mended the engines that ran the Great Northern.

stories.headline: The City of Destiny vs. The Emerald City: How a Telegram Changed Northwest History
stories.dek: A telegram named Tacoma the terminus in 1873 and Seattle took it about as well as you'd expect, then spent thirty years proving the railroad wrong.

stories.headline: When the Railroad Came for Yakama Land: Broken Treaties and the Birth of Two Cities
stories.dek: A promise made to Chief Kamiakin in 1853 didn't survive the season, and thirty years later the same railroad picked up a whole town and carried it four miles north.

stories.headline: The Night They Drove Out Chinatown: Seattle's 1886 Anti-Chinese Riots
stories.dek: A mob of 1,500 rounded up Seattle's Chinese residents for forced deportation in February 1886, three months after Tacoma showed the coast how it was done.

stories.headline: The Builders History Forgot: Chinese Workers of the Northern Pacific
stories.dek: Two-thirds of the crews that built the western line were Chinese. They closed the last gap in Montana, and the country left them out of the painting.

stories.headline: When Labor Beat the Empire Builder: The Great Northern Strike of 1894
stories.dek: For eighteen days in April 1894 a ten-month-old union stopped James J. Hill's railroad cold and won back nearly every dollar he had cut.

stories.headline: Empire Builder vs. Railroad King: The Battle That Nearly Crashed Wall Street
stories.dek: Hill and Harriman fought for the Northern Pacific until it hit $1,000 a share and dragged the whole market down with it.

stories.headline: The Blind Pool: The Rise and Fall of Henry Villard
stories.dek: He raised millions without telling anyone what he was buying, took the Northern Pacific by ambush, and lost it four months after the golden spike.

stories.headline: The One-Eyed Empire Builder: James J. Hill and the Railroad That Never Went Broke
stories.dek: Half blind and broke at eighteen, he laid the only transcontinental built without public money, and the only one that never went bankrupt.

stories.headline: The Columbia River Gorge: One River, Two Railroads, Two Titans
stories.dek: The only water-level door through the Cascades, and two railroad kings raced to own both banks of it.

stories.headline: Two Trains, One Track: The Wreck That Invented Modern Management
stories.dek: A head-on collision on a single Massachusetts track in 1841 gave us the modern org chart. The AI boom is about to test it.

stories.headline: The Switchback Era: When Trains Traveled 13 Miles to Move 3
stories.dek: Before the tunnel, the Great Northern climbed Stevens Pass on eight switchbacks, backing over the summit at four percent.

stories.headline: Conquering the Cascades: The Eight-Mile Tunnel That Answered Wellington
stories.dek: Bored 7.8 miles through granite in three years, the 1929 Cascade Tunnel took Great Northern's trains down off the killing slopes for good.

stories.headline: Massacre at Deep Creek: The Slaughter the Canyon Hid for a Century
stories.dek: In 1887, at least 31 Chinese gold miners were murdered in Hells Canyon. No one was ever convicted.

stories.headline: Three Days Apart: The Twin Railroad Avalanches of 1910
stories.dek: Seventy-two hours after Wellington, the Selkirks took 58 more men — the deadliest week the high iron ever knew.

stories.headline: White Death at Wellington
stories.dek: March 1, 1910 — an avalanche swept two Great Northern trains into a canyon, killing 96. The deadliest avalanche in U.S. history.

stories.headline: The Deschutes Canyon Railroad War
stories.dek: Dynamite, sharpshooters, and hand-to-hand combat as two railroad titans warred up Oregon's Deschutes Canyon.

stories.headline: The Night He Walked Alone: John F. Stevens' Discovery of Marias Pass
stories.dek: Alone in a Montana blizzard, John F. Stevens found the pass that completed a transcontinental dream.

stories.headline: Stampede Pass: The $1,000 Race Through the Mountain
stories.dek: Two crews bored a mountain from opposite sides, racing for a $1,000 prize and the future of Puget Sound.

stories.headline: The Great Big Baked Potato
stories.dek: How the Northern Pacific turned an Idaho spud into the most famous meal on American rails.
